turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I am not here to threaten you, Sandip. My concerns are legitimate, and I will not hesitate to protect my people from any form of oppression, regardless of the source.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Your concerns are as baseless as your threats, Nikhil. I am not cowed by the likes of you or any local Muslims. As for your tenantry, they are free to choose their own path, and if they find my influence more liberating than yours, I see no wrong in that.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your influence may seem liberating to some, Sandip, but it is a dangerous illusion. I will not stand idly by while you exploit my people.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Exploit my people, you say? Nikhil, my dear rival, you know nothing of the fire that burns within your tenants. They are not sheep to be shepherded but warriors ready to rise. And as for your threats, I laugh at them. The day you can quell the spirit of the people is the day you can command the wind to cease blowing.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I see through your illusions, Sandip. The spirit of the people you speak of is not one of true liberation, but of manipulation and fear. I will protect my people from your false promises.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I am torn between you both, Sandip, Nikhil. Your words strike me deeply, yet I cannot choose sides. The truth seems to hide in shadows.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Bimala, my beloved, your heart is as conflicted as the times we live in. But fear not the shadows; they are but the void awaiting the light of truth. My promises, though you call them false, are the beacon guiding the people from the tyranny of ignorance and oppression.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Sandip, your words touch my heart, yet Nikhil's concerns weigh on my mind. How can I find the truth when both of you see it so differently?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your words may sway hearts, Sandip, but they do not change the reality of oppression and division. I come here not to argue but to demand that you cease your harmful actions against my people.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, Nikhil, your concerns are as predictable as they are misplaced. I have no need to cease actions that are the breath of freedom for the oppressed. And yet, I understand your fear; it is the shadow of your own soul, reflecting the darkness you seek to impose on others.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your words may be grand, Sandip, but they ring hollow to those who suffer under your guise of freedom. I warn you now: continue this path, and you will face more than just my disapproval.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Nikhil, your warnings are but the echo of a fading era. I speak not just with my tongue but with the pulse of the people. It is they who will determine the truth of my actions, not the shadows that cling to the past.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your pulse, Sandip, beats to the rhythm of your own delusions. The people will see through your facade when the reality of your actions confronts them.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: The people's hearts are not so easily swayed by shadows, Nikhil. They see the light of truth in my words and actions, a truth you fear to acknowledge.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your light, Sandip, is but the flicker of a match in a storm. The truth you speak is drowned by the screams of those you oppress.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Nikhil, your words are like the whispers of the timid. I am the voice of the masses, their champion in the face of oppression. The storm you speak of is but a breeze to my flame.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your flame, Sandip, is but a spark in the night. It will be extinguished by the storm that is the truth of your tyranny.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Nikhil, your thunderous rhetoric is but the echo of your fear. The people see through your cowardice and embrace the light of my truth.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your truth, Sandip, is but the smoke of your lies. The people will see the fire for what it truly is when the wind of reality blows it away.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Nikhil, your words are like the shadows that dance in the corner when the light of truth shines bright. The people see through your veils of righteousness and find solace in the warmth of my passion.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ... No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
